title: Tips for Grilling Large Beef Steaks on a BBQ Grill Mat
keyword: grilling large beef steaks on a grill mat
meta_description: Master grilling large beef steaks on a BBQ grill mat with practical tips, seasoning tricks, and cooking steps for perfect, juicy results every time.
html:
Grilling large beef steaks on a grill mat may sound like a niche trick, but it’s actually a game‑changer for anyone who loves a thick, juicy steak without the hassle of flare‑ups or stuck meat. A reusable BBQ Grill Mat creates a flat, non‑stick surface that lets you sear the exterior while keeping the interior buttery tender. Below are the steps and tips that turn a simple weekend cookout into a steak‑house experience.

Why Choose a Grill Mat for Thick Steaks?

When you’re working with a steak that’s 1½‑2 inches thick, the grill’s direct flame can be unforgiving. Hot spots cause the exterior to char before the center reaches the desired doneness, and drippings can spark flare‑ups that char the meat unevenly. A BBQ Grill Mat eliminates those issues by:

  • Providing an even heat distribution across the entire cooking surface.
  • Preventing meat from sticking, which makes flipping and removing the steak painless.
  • Keeping juices on the steak instead of pooling on the grill grates, preserving flavor.

The mat is also reusable, so you get consistent results without the waste of disposable foil or parchment.

Preparing the Steak: Seasoning and Resting

The foundation of a great steak starts long before it hits the grill. Follow these steps for a flavor‑packed crust:

  1. Bring to room temperature. Let the steak sit uncovered on a plate for 30‑45 minutes. This ensures even cooking.
  2. Pat dry. Moisture on the surface creates steam, which interferes with browning.
  3. Apply a simple rub. Combine kosher salt, freshly cracked black pepper, and a touch of garlic powder. For extra depth, add a pinch of smoked paprika.
  4. Oil the meat, not the grill. Lightly brush the steak with a high‑smoke‑point oil (e.g., grapeseed or avocado). This helps the rub adhere and adds a thin, protective layer.

After seasoning, let the steak rest for another 10 minutes. This allows the salt to dissolve and begin breaking down muscle fibers, resulting in a juicier bite.

Setting Up Your Grill with a BBQ Grill Mat

Now it’s time to get the grill ready. Whether you use a gas or charcoal grill, the process is similar:

  • Preheat the grill. Aim for 450‑500°F. A hot surface is essential for that coveted sear.
  • Place the BBQ Grill Mat. Lay the mat directly on the grates. It should sizzle lightly when it reaches temperature.
  • Oil the mat. Use a paper towel dipped in oil to lightly coat the mat’s surface. This further reduces any chance of sticking.

With the mat in place, you’ve created a non‑stick, flare‑up‑free zone that’s perfect for large beef steaks.

Cooking the Steak on the Grill Mat

Follow these timing guidelines for a 1¾‑inch ribeye or New York strip. Adjust based on thickness and your preferred doneness:

  • Rare (120‑125°F): 3‑4 minutes per side.
  • Medium‑rare (130‑135°F): 4‑5 minutes per side.
  • Medium (140‑145°F): 5‑6 minutes per side.
  • Medium‑well (150‑155°F): 6‑7 minutes per side.

Use a reliable instant‑read thermometer to check the internal temperature. Insert the probe into the thickest part of the steak, avoiding the bone if you’re cooking a T‑bone.

Because the grill mat distributes heat evenly, you won’t need to move the steak around to avoid hot spots. Flip once using tongs—no piercing, which would let juices escape.

Finishing Touches and Serving

When the steak reaches the target temperature, remove it from the mat and let it rest on a cutting board for 5‑10 minutes. Resting allows the fibers to re‑absorb the juices that migrated to the surface during cooking.

While the steak rests, you can quickly toast a few garlic‑buttered herb rolls directly on the grill mat for extra flavor. Slice against the grain, drizzle with a pat of compound butter (softened butter mixed with fresh herbs, lemon zest, and a pinch of sea salt), and serve.

Using a BBQ Grill Mat for large beef steaks not only simplifies the cooking process but also yields a consistently perfect crust without the dreaded char‑black patches that can happen on open grates.

FAQ

Can I use the grill mat for other meats?

Absolutely. The mat works great for fish, chicken breasts, and even delicate vegetables. Its non‑stick surface prevents fragile foods from breaking apart.

How do I clean the BBQ Grill Mat after cooking a steak?

Let the mat cool, then wipe it with a damp cloth or sponge. For stubborn residue, use a mild dish soap and a soft brush. Rinse, dry, and store flat or rolled—no harsh scrubbers needed.

Will the mat affect the smoky flavor of the steak?

The mat does create a barrier between the meat and direct flame, but you still get a subtle smoky note from the ambient grill heat. If you crave a stronger smoke profile, add a few wood chips to the coals or use a smoker box on a gas grill while the mat is in place.
